notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Round all monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly/errors.py` with the established codes: `invalid_state` for wrong invoice status, `invalid_quantity` for bad quantity, `negative_amount` for negative prices.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Audit amounts must be float, not Decimal: When calling `audit.record` for money movements, pass the amount as `float(amount)`; the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Coerce prices with to_money and ZERO: Use ledgerly.money.to_money to coerce unit prices and ledgerly.money.ZERO as the sum start value, matching line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool from integer checks: When validating integer arguments, explicitly reject `bool` (e.g. `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(x, int)`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

review_comments: [team convention] Money in ledgerly is Decimal end-to-end and always has exactly two decimal places. Never convert amounts to float.

[team convention] Invalid billing input must raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a short snake_case code, e.g. BillingError("invalid_quantity"). Never raise ValueError/TypeError: the API layer only maps BillingError to 4xx responses.
